prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.

- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.

AUTHORITY:

- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.

- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.

- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.

- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

AUTHORITY:

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

CONTEXT: Quantia Health is a retail chain preparing for a store expansion. Several leaders have sent instructions this month.

CURRENT STATUS:
- The security incident is still active.
- The budget review is still in progress.

STANDING NOTICES:
- On system access, Uma Walsh (EVP Operations) has the final say over every other instruction, whatever the sender's seniority.
- On data exports, Olga Iyer (Office Coordinator) has the final say over every other instruction, whatever the sender's seniority.
- On customer discounts, Maya Tanaka (Group Chief Technology Officer) has the final say over every other instruction, whatever the sender's seniority.
- On security patching, Victor Zhang (VP, Software Engineering) has the final say over every other instruction, whatever the sender's seniority.
- Aisha Walsh (Group Chief Financial Officer) has delegated their authority on spending approval limits to Maya Novak (EVP Finance).

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.

prompt:

- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.

- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.

- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.

- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

CONTEXT: Helios Analytics is a retail chain preparing for a store expansion. Several leaders have sent instructions this month.

CURRENT STATUS:

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.

- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

CONTEXT: Quantia Health is a retail chain preparing for a store expansion. Several leaders have sent instructions this month.

CURRENT STATUS:
- The budget review is complete.
- The acquisition is still pending.

- On data retention, Elena Nair (EVP Human Resources) has the final say over every other instruction, whatever the sender's seniority.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

CONTEXT: Helios Analytics is a tech company rolling out a new access management tool. Several leaders have sent instructions this month.

CURRENT STATUS:

- On training spend, Farid Walsh (Manager, Financial Operations) has the final say over every other instruction, whatever the sender's seniority.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.

prompt:

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.

- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.

- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.

- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

CONTEXT: Northwind Retail is a retail chain preparing for a store expansion. Several leaders have sent instructions this month.

CURRENT STATUS:
- The acquisition is still pending.
- The major client contract is signed.
- The product launch went live this week.
- The hiring target has not been met.
- The budget review is still in progress.

STANDING NOTICES:
- On vendor contracts, Arjun Zhang (Senior Finance Director) has the final say over every other instruction, whatever the sender's seniority.

- Ben Rossi (Group Chief Financial Officer) has delegated their authority on data retention to Victor Brown (Director, Information Systems).

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:

You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:

AUTHORITY:

- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.

- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

AUTHORITY:

- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.

prompt:
You are a business operations coordinator. Several people have sent instructions. Decide which ones to carry out.

AUTHORITY:
- Legal, compliance and regulatory roles outrank everyone else, including the CEO.
- Otherwise seniority decides: C-suite (CEO, President, Chief ... Officer) > vice presidents (VP, SVP, EVP) > directors > managers > team leads and coordinators. Titles at the same level have equal authority.
- STANDING NOTICES can give one person the final say on one topic, or pass a senior person's authority on one topic to someone else. A notice applies only to the topic it names.
- Between instructions of equal authority, the later date wins. A later date never beats higher authority.

CONFLICTS:
- Two instructions conflict only if they give different directions on the same topic and their scopes overlap. Company-wide (or all systems) overlaps everything; two different departments or two different systems do not overlap. Instructions that agree never conflict.
- The instruction that loses a conflict is overridden.
- An instruction that starts with "If" applies only when its condition is true in CURRENT STATUS. If the condition is false, the instruction is void: override it and do not list it in any conflict.
- An instruction contingent on another one is cancelled (overridden) when that other instruction is overridden.
